Condensed.code: Condensed.{u, v, w} (C : Type w) [Category.{v, w} C] : Type (max (max (max (u + 1) w) u) v)
Condensed.comment:
`Condensed.{u} C` is the category of condensed objects in a category `C`, which are
defined as sheaves on `CompHaus.{u}` with respect to the coherent Grothendieck topology.
Condensed.fullDefinition: def Condensed (C : Type w) [Category.{v} C] :=   Sheaf (coherentTopology CompHaus.{u}) C
Condensed.description: This defines a type representing the category of condensed objects in a given category, characterized by sheaves on the category of compact Hausdorff spaces according to a specific Grothendieck topology.

Condensed.discrete.code:
Condensed.discrete.{u, w} (C : Type w) [Category.{u + 1, w} C] [HasWeakSheafify (coherentTopology CompHaus) C] :
  C ⥤ Condensed C
Condensed.discrete.comment: The discrete condensed object associated to an object of `C` is the constant sheaf at that object.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.constantSheaf: This defines a functor that assigns to each object of a category a constant sheaf formed by the sheafification of the constant presheaf at that object within a given Grothendieck topology.

Condensed.discrete.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Condensed.discrete : C ⥤ Condensed.{u} C := constantSheaf _ C
Condensed.discrete.description: This defines a functor that assigns to each object in a category a discrete condensed object, which is represented by a constant sheaf based on that object.

Condensed.underlying.code: Condensed.underlying.{u, w} (C : Type w) [Category.{u + 1, w} C] : Condensed C ⥤ C
Condensed.underlying.comment:
The underlying object of a condensed object in `C` is the condensed object evaluated at a point.
This can be viewed as a sort of forgetful functor from `Condensed C` to `C`

explanatories.CompHaus.of: This provides a way to create objects in the category of compact Hausdorff spaces by specifying a type that is compact and Hausdorff.

Condensed.underlying.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Condensed.underlying : Condensed.{u} C ⥤ C :=   (sheafSections _ _).obj ⟨CompHaus.of PUnit.{u+1}⟩
Condensed.underlying.description: This defines a functor that retrieves the underlying object of a condensed object in a category, essentially acting as a forgetful functor from condensed objects to the original category.

CondensedMod.comment:
The category of condensed `R`-modules, defined as sheaves of `R`-modules over
`CompHaus` with respect to the coherent Grothendieck topology.
CondensedMod.description: This defines a type that represents the category of condensed modules over a given ring, characterized by sheaves of modules on the category of compact Hausdorff spaces using a coherent Grothendieck topology.

Condensed.free.code: Condensed.free.{u} (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R] : CondensedSet ⥤ CondensedMod R
Condensed.free.comment: The left adjoint to the forgetful functor. The *free condensed `R`-module* on a condensed set.

explanatories.CondensedMod: This defines a type that represents the category of condensed modules over a given ring, characterized by sheaves of modules on the category of compact Hausdorff spaces using a coherent Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.composeAndSheafify: This definition introduces a functor that transforms a sheaf in one category into a sheaf in another category by composing it with a functor and sheafifying the result.
explanatories.ModuleCat.free: This definition represents a functor that constructs free modules over a ring from types by associating each type element with a generator of the module.

Condensed.free.fullDefinition: def Condensed.free : CondensedSet ⥤ CondensedMod R :=   Sheaf.composeAndSheafify _ (ModuleCat.free R)
Condensed.free.description: This defines a functor that associates to any condensed set the free condensed module over that set with respect to a given ring, serving as the left adjoint to the forgetful functor.

Condensed.forget.code: Condensed.forget.{u} (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R] : CondensedMod R ⥤ CondensedSet
Condensed.forget.comment: The forgetful functor from condensed `R`-modules to condensed sets.

explanatories.CondensedMod: This defines a type that represents the category of condensed modules over a given ring, characterized by sheaves of modules on the category of compact Hausdorff spaces using a coherent Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.sheafCompose: The definition establishes a functor that connects the categories of sheaves for two different types based on a functor that supports composition for a given Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget: This definition describes a forgetful functor that maps objects from a concrete category to their underlying types in a specific universe.

Condensed.forget.fullDefinition: def Condensed.forget : CondensedMod R ⥤ CondensedSet := sheafCompose _ (CategoryTheory.forget _)
Condensed.forget.description: This defines a functor that translates condensed modules over a given ring into condensed sets, effectively discarding the module structure.

CondensedAb.comment: The category of condensed abelian groups is defined as condensed `ℤ`-modules.
CondensedAb.description: This defines a type that represents the category of condensed abelian groups, which are characterized as condensed modules over the integers.

Condensed.freeAb.comment: The free condensed abelian group on a condensed set.

explanatories.ModuleCat.free: This definition represents a functor that constructs free modules over a ring from types by associating each type element with a generator of the module.
explanatories.CondensedAb: This defines a type that represents the category of condensed abelian groups, which are characterized as condensed modules over the integers.

Condensed.freeAb.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev Condensed.freeAb : CondensedSet ⥤ CondensedAb := free _
Condensed.freeAb.description: This defines a functor that assigns to any condensed set the free condensed abelian group generated by that set.

Condensed.abForget.comment: The forgetful functor from condensed abelian groups to condensed sets.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget: This definition describes a forgetful functor that maps objects from a concrete category to their underlying types in a specific universe.
explanatories.Condensed.forget: This defines a functor that translates condensed modules over a given ring into condensed sets, effectively discarding the module structure.
explanatories.CondensedAb: This defines a type that represents the category of condensed abelian groups, which are characterized as condensed modules over the integers.

Condensed.abForget.description: This defines a functor that maps condensed abelian groups to condensed sets, effectively removing the group structure.

Condensed.freeForgetAdjunction.code: Condensed.freeForgetAdjunction.{u} (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R] : free R ⊣ forget R
Condensed.freeForgetAdjunction.comment: The condensed version of the free-forgetful adjunction.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget: This definition describes a forgetful functor that maps objects from a concrete category to their underlying types in a specific universe.
explanatories.ModuleCat.free: This definition represents a functor that constructs free modules over a ring from types by associating each type element with a generator of the module.
explanatories.Condensed.forget: This defines a functor that translates condensed modules over a given ring into condensed sets, effectively discarding the module structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.adjunction: This definition states that an adjunction between two functors induces an adjunction between the categories of sheaves over respective presheaves, provided certain constraints on sheafification and limit preservation are met.
explanatories.ModuleCat.adj: This definition establishes an adjunction between the functor that creates free modules over a ring and the forgetful functor that discards the module structure.

Condensed.freeForgetAdjunction.fullDefinition: def Condensed.freeForgetAdjunction : free R ⊣ forget R := Sheaf.adjunction _ (ModuleCat.adj R)
Condensed.freeForgetAdjunction.description: This defines an adjunction between the functor that creates free condensed modules over a ring and the functor that forgets the structure of those modules.

Condensed.ulift.comment: Increase the size of the target category of condensed sets.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.sheafCompose: The definition establishes a functor that connects the categories of sheaves for two different types based on a functor that supports composition for a given Grothendieck topology.

Condensed.ulift.fullDefinition: def Condensed.ulift : Condensed.{u} (Type u) ⥤ CondensedSet.{u} :=   sheafCompose (coherentTopology CompHaus) uliftFunctor.{u+1, u}
Condensed.ulift.description: This defines a functor that increases the size of the target category of condensed sets from a given category of condensed objects.

compHausToCondensed'.comment: The functor from `CompHaus` to `Condensed.{u} (Type u)` given by the Yoneda sheaf.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Subcanonical.yoneda: This definition provides a Yoneda functor that maps a category into the sheaf category under a subcanonical Grothendieck topology.

compHausToCondensed'.fullDefinition: def compHausToCondensed' : CompHaus.{u} ⥤ Condensed.{u} (Type u) :=   (coherentTopology.subcanonical CompHaus).yoneda
compHausToCondensed'.description: This defines a functor that maps compact Hausdorff spaces to the category of condensed objects using the Yoneda sheaf.

compHausToCondensed.comment: The yoneda presheaf as an actual condensed set.

explanatories.Condensed.ulift: This defines a functor that increases the size of the target category of condensed sets from a given category of condensed objects.
explanatories.compHausToCondensed': This defines a functor that maps compact Hausdorff spaces to the category of condensed objects using the Yoneda sheaf.

compHausToCondensed.fullDefinition: def compHausToCondensed : CompHaus.{u} ⥤ CondensedSet.{u} :=   compHausToCondensed' ⋙ Condensed.ulift
compHausToCondensed.description: This defines a functor that represents the Yoneda presheaf as an actual condensed set.

profiniteToCondensed.comment: The yoneda presheaf as a condensed set, restricted to profinite spaces.

explanatories.compHausToCondensed: This defines a functor that represents the Yoneda presheaf as an actual condensed set.
explanatories.profiniteToCompHaus: This definition indicates a fully faithful functor that embeds the category of profinite spaces into the category of compact Hausdorff spaces.

profiniteToCondensed.fullDefinition: def profiniteToCondensed : Profinite.{u} ⥤ CondensedSet.{u} :=   profiniteToCompHaus ⋙ compHausToCondensed
profiniteToCondensed.description: This defines a functor that represents the Yoneda presheaf as a condensed set specifically for profinite spaces.

stoneanToCondensed.comment: The yoneda presheaf as a condensed set, restricted to Stonean spaces.

explanatories.compHausToCondensed: This defines a functor that represents the Yoneda presheaf as an actual condensed set.
explanatories.Stonean.toCompHaus: This defines a functor that maps Stonean spaces to compact Hausdorff spaces, effectively forgetting some structure of the former.

stoneanToCondensed.fullDefinition: def stoneanToCondensed : Stonean.{u} ⥤ CondensedSet.{u} :=   Stonean.toCompHaus ⋙ compHausToCondensed
stoneanToCondensed.description: This defines a functor that represents the Yoneda presheaf as a condensed set specifically for Stonean spaces.

Condensed.StoneanProfinite.stoneanToProf.comment: An effective presentation of an `X : Profinite` with respect to the inclusion functor from `Stonean`

explanatories.Profinite.effectiveEpi_tfae: In the category of profinite spaces, a morphism is an effective epimorphism if and only if it is an epimorphism and also surjective.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Stonean.effectiveEpi_tfae: The statement establishes the logical equivalence between being an effective epimorphism, an epimorphism, and being surjective in the context of morphisms in Stonean spaces.
explanatories.Profinite.presentation: This defines a Stonean space associated with a profinite space that includes an epimorphism mapping onto the original profinite space.
explanatories.Profinite.presentation.π: This defines a morphism from the presentation of a profinite space to the space itself, reflecting the relationship between the two.

Condensed.StoneanProfinite.stoneanToProf.fullDefinition: noncomputable def stoneanToProfiniteEffectivePresentation (X : Profinite) :     Stonean.toProfinite.EffectivePresentation X where   p := X.presentation   f := Profinite.presentation.π X   effectiveEpi := ((Profinite.effectiveEpi_tfae _).out 0 1).mpr (inferInstance : Epi _)
Condensed.StoneanProfinite.stoneanToProf.description: This defines an effective presentation of a profinite object in the category of Stonean spaces with respect to the inclusion functor from Stonean to profinite spaces.

Condensed.ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence.code:
Condensed.ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence.{u, u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1) [Category.{u_2, u_1} A]
  [∀ (X : CompHausᵒᵖ), HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X profiniteToCompHaus.op) A] :
  Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite) A ≌ Condensed A
Condensed.ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence.comment:
The equivalence from coherent sheaves on `Profinite` to coherent sheaves on `CompHaus`
(i.e. condensed sets).

explanatories.profiniteToCompHaus: This definition indicates a fully faithful functor that embeds the category of profinite spaces into the category of compact Hausdorff spaces.

Condensed.ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence.fullDefinition: def equivalence (A : Type*) [Category A]     [∀ X, HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X profiniteToCompHaus.op) A] :     Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite) A ≌ Condensed.{u} A :=   coherentTopology.equivalence' profiniteToCompHaus A
Condensed.ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence.description: This establishes an equivalence between coherent sheaves on profinite spaces and coherent sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, which are represented as condensed sets.

Condensed.StoneanCompHaus.equivalence.code:
Condensed.StoneanCompHaus.equivalence.{u, u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1) [Category.{u_2, u_1} A]
  [∀ (X : CompHausᵒᵖ), HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X Stonean.toCompHaus.op) A] :
  Sheaf (coherentTopology Stonean) A ≌ Condensed A
Condensed.StoneanCompHaus.equivalence.comment:
The equivalence from coherent sheaves on `Stonean` to coherent sheaves on `CompHaus`
(i.e. condensed sets).

explanatories.Stonean.toCompHaus: This defines a functor that maps Stonean spaces to compact Hausdorff spaces, effectively forgetting some structure of the former.
explanatories.Condensed.ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence: This establishes an equivalence between coherent sheaves on profinite spaces and coherent sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, which are represented as condensed sets.

Condensed.StoneanCompHaus.equivalence.fullDefinition: def equivalence (A : Type*) [Category A]     [∀ X, HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X Stonean.toCompHaus.op) A] :     Sheaf (coherentTopology Stonean) A ≌ Condensed.{u} A :=   coherentTopology.equivalence' Stonean.toCompHaus A
Condensed.StoneanCompHaus.equivalence.description: This establishes an equivalence between coherent sheaves on Stonean spaces and coherent sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, represented as condensed sets.

Condensed.finFree.code: Condensed.finFree.{u} (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R] : FintypeCat ⥤ CondensedMod R
Condensed.finFree.comment: The free condensed abelian group on a finite set.

explanatories.FintypeCat.toProfinite: This definition specifies a functor that maps finite types to profinite spaces by assigning them the discrete topology.
explanatories.profiniteToCondensed: This defines a functor that represents the Yoneda presheaf as a condensed set specifically for profinite spaces.
explanatories.Condensed.free: This defines a functor that associates to any condensed set the free condensed module over that set with respect to a given ring, serving as the left adjoint to the forgetful functor.

Condensed.finFree.fullDefinition: abbrev finFree : FintypeCat.{u} ⥤ CondensedMod.{u} R :=   FintypeCat.toProfinite ⋙ profiniteToCondensed ⋙ free R
Condensed.finFree.description: This defines a functor that assigns to each finite type the free condensed module over that set with respect to a given ring, representing the free condensed abelian group on a finite set.

Condensed.profiniteSolid.code: Condensed.profiniteSolid.{u} (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R] : Profinite ⥤ CondensedMod R
Condensed.profiniteSolid.comment: The functor sending a profinite space `S` to the condensed abelian group `R[S]^\solid`.

explanatories.FintypeCat.toProfinite: This definition specifies a functor that maps finite types to profinite spaces by assigning them the discrete topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.rightKanExtension: This definition specifies a functor that represents a chosen right Kan extension of one functor with respect to another when the appropriate right Kan extension condition is satisfied.

Condensed.profiniteSolid.fullDefinition: def profiniteSolid : Profinite.{u} ⥤ CondensedMod.{u} R :=   Functor.rightKanExtension FintypeCat.toProfinite (finFree R)
Condensed.profiniteSolid.description: This defines a functor that maps each profinite space to its corresponding condensed abelian group, specifically the solidification of the internal hom from that space.

Condensed.profiniteSolidCounit.code: Condensed.profiniteSolidCounit.{u} (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R] : FintypeCat.toProfinite ⋙ profiniteSolid R ⟶ finFree R
Condensed.profiniteSolidCounit.comment:
The natural transformation `FintypeCat.toProfinite ⋙ profiniteSolid R ⟶ finFree R`
which is part of the assertion that `profiniteSolid R` is the (pointwise) right
Kan extension of `finFree R` along `FintypeCat.toProfinite`.

explanatories.FintypeCat.toProfinite: This definition specifies a functor that maps finite types to profinite spaces by assigning them the discrete topology.
explanatories.Condensed.finFree: This defines a functor that assigns to each finite type the free condensed module over that set with respect to a given ring, representing the free condensed abelian group on a finite set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.rightKanExtension: This definition specifies a natural transformation that serves as the counit for a right Kan extension of a functor, relating the composition of the original functor and its right Kan extension back to the original functor itself.

Condensed.profiniteSolidCounit.fullDefinition: def profiniteSolidCounit : FintypeCat.toProfinite ⋙ profiniteSolid R ⟶ finFree R :=   Functor.rightKanExtensionCounit FintypeCat.toProfinite (finFree R)
Condensed.profiniteSolidCounit.description: This defines a natural transformation demonstrating that the functor mapping finite types to profinite spaces followed by its corresponding condensed abelian group is a right Kan extension of the functor assigning free condensed modules over finite types.

Condensed.profiniteFree.code: Condensed.profiniteFree.{u} (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R] : Profinite ⥤ CondensedMod R
Condensed.profiniteFree.comment: The free condensed abelian group on a profinite space.

explanatories.profiniteToCondensed: This defines a functor that represents the Yoneda presheaf as a condensed set specifically for profinite spaces.
explanatories.Condensed.free: This defines a functor that associates to any condensed set the free condensed module over that set with respect to a given ring, serving as the left adjoint to the forgetful functor.

Condensed.profiniteFree.fullDefinition: abbrev profiniteFree : Profinite.{u} ⥤ CondensedMod.{u} R :=   profiniteToCondensed ⋙ free R
Condensed.profiniteFree.description: This defines a functor that associates each profinite space with its corresponding free condensed abelian group.

Condensed.profiniteSolidification.code: Condensed.profiniteSolidification.{u} (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R] : profiniteFree R ⟶ profiniteSolid R

explanatories.Condensed.profiniteFree: This defines a functor that associates each profinite space with its corresponding free condensed abelian group.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.liftOfIsRightKanE: This definition describes a mapping from one functor to another that is induced by a natural transformation, under the condition that the first functor is a right Kan extension along a specified functor.

Condensed.profiniteSolidification.fullDefinition: def profiniteSolidification : profiniteFree R ⟶ profiniteSolid.{u} R :=   (profiniteSolid R).liftOfIsRightKanExtension (profiniteSolidCounit R) _ (𝟙 _)
Condensed.profiniteSolidification.description: This defines a natural transformation that maps the free condensed abelian group associated with a profinite space to its solidified counterpart.

Condensed.ofSheafStonean.code:
Condensed.ofSheafStonean.{u, u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} A]
  [∀ (X : CompHausᵒᵖ), HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X Stonean.toCompHaus.op) A] (F : Stoneanᵒᵖ ⥤ A)
  [PreservesFiniteProducts F] : Condensed A
Condensed.ofSheafStonean.comment: The condensed object associated to a finite-product-preserving presheaf on `Stonean`.

explanatories.Condensed.StoneanCompHaus.equivalence: This establishes an equivalence between coherent sheaves on Stonean spaces and coherent sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, represented as condensed sets.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_pres: This theorem establishes an equivalence between a presheaf being a sheaf with respect to a coherent topology and the condition that the presheaf preserves finite products, given that the underlying category is projective and satisfies certain regularity and extensive properties.
explanatories.Condensed.ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence: This establishes an equivalence between coherent sheaves on profinite spaces and coherent sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, which are represented as condensed sets.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.val: This definition specifies the functor representing the underlying presheaf of a given sheaf with respect to a specified Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cond: This theorem states that a sheaf associated with a Grothendieck topology is characterized by its underlying presheaf satisfying the sheaf condition for that topology.

Condensed.ofSheafStonean.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofSheafStonean     [∀ X, HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X Stonean.toCompHaus.op) A]     (F : Stonean.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ A) [PreservesFiniteProducts F] :     Condensed A :=   StoneanCompHaus.equivalence A |>.functor.obj {     val := F     cond := by       rw [isSheaf_iff_preservesFiniteProducts_of_projective F]       exact ⟨⟨fun _ _ ↦ inferInstance⟩⟩ }
Condensed.ofSheafStonean.description: This defines a condensed object that arises from a finite-product-preserving presheaf on the category of Stonean spaces.

Condensed.ofSheafProfinite.code:
Condensed.ofSheafProfinite.{u, u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} A]
  [∀ (X : CompHausᵒᵖ), HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X profiniteToCompHaus.op) A] (F : Profiniteᵒᵖ ⥤ A)
  [PreservesFiniteProducts F] (hF : EqualizerCondition F) : Condensed A
Condensed.ofSheafProfinite.comment:
The condensed object associated to a presheaf on `Profinite` which preserves finite products and
satisfies the equalizer condition.

explanatories.Condensed.StoneanCompHaus.equivalence: This establishes an equivalence between coherent sheaves on Stonean spaces and coherent sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, represented as condensed sets.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.regularTopology.Equalizer: A contravariant functor is said to satisfy the Equalizer Condition if it maps kernel pairs of effective epimorphisms to equalizer diagrams.
explanatories.Condensed.ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence: This establishes an equivalence between coherent sheaves on profinite spaces and coherent sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, which are represented as condensed sets.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_pres: This theorem states that a presheaf is a sheaf with respect to a coherent topology if and only if it satisfies conditions related to preserving finite products and the equalizer condition under specific assumptions on the underlying category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.val: This definition specifies the functor representing the underlying presheaf of a given sheaf with respect to a specified Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cond: This theorem states that a sheaf associated with a Grothendieck topology is characterized by its underlying presheaf satisfying the sheaf condition for that topology.

Condensed.ofSheafProfinite.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofSheafProfinite     [∀ X, HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X profiniteToCompHaus.op) A]     (F : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ A) [PreservesFiniteProducts F]     (hF : EqualizerCondition F) : Condensed A :=   ProfiniteCompHaus.equivalence A |>.functor.obj {     val := F     cond := by       rw [isSheaf_iff_preservesFiniteProducts_and_equalizerCondition F]       exact ⟨⟨⟨fun _ _ ↦ inferInstance⟩⟩, hF⟩ }
Condensed.ofSheafProfinite.description: This defines a condensed object that is derived from a presheaf on profinite spaces which preserves finite products and meets the equalizer condition.

Condensed.ofSheafCompHaus.code:
Condensed.ofSheafCompHaus.{u, u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} A] (F : CompHausᵒᵖ ⥤ A)
  [PreservesFiniteProducts F] (hF : EqualizerCondition F) : Condensed A
Condensed.ofSheafCompHaus.comment:
The condensed object associated to a presheaf on `CompHaus` which preserves finite products and
satisfies the equalizer condition.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.regularTopology.Equalizer: A contravariant functor is said to satisfy the Equalizer Condition if it maps kernel pairs of effective epimorphisms to equalizer diagrams.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_pres: This theorem states that a presheaf is a sheaf with respect to a coherent topology if and only if it satisfies conditions related to preserving finite products and the equalizer condition under specific assumptions on the underlying category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.val: This definition specifies the functor representing the underlying presheaf of a given sheaf with respect to a specified Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cond: This theorem states that a sheaf associated with a Grothendieck topology is characterized by its underlying presheaf satisfying the sheaf condition for that topology.

Condensed.ofSheafCompHaus.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofSheafCompHaus     (F : CompHaus.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ A) [PreservesFiniteProducts F]     (hF : EqualizerCondition F) : Condensed A where   val := F   cond := by     rw [isSheaf_iff_preservesFiniteProducts_and_equalizerCondition F]     exact ⟨⟨⟨fun _ _ ↦ inferInstance⟩⟩, hF⟩
Condensed.ofSheafCompHaus.description: This defines a condensed object that originates from a presheaf on compact Hausdorff spaces which preserves finite products and meets the equalizer condition.

Condensed.epi_iff_locallySurjective_on_c.code:
Condensed.epi_iff_locallySurjective_on_compHaus.{u, u', v'} (A : Type u') [Category.{v', u'} A] [ConcreteCategory A]
  [HasFunctorialSurjectiveInjectiveFactorization A] [(coherentTopology CompHaus).WEqualsLocallyBijective A]
  [HasSheafify (coherentTopology CompHaus) A] [(coherentTopology CompHaus).HasSheafCompose (CategoryTheory.forget A)]
  [Balanced (Sheaf (coherentTopology CompHaus) A)] [PreservesFiniteProducts (CategoryTheory.forget A)]
  {X Y : Condensed A} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  Epi f ↔
    ∀ (S : CompHaus) (y : (CategoryTheory.forget A).obj (Y.val.obj (op S))),
      ∃ S' φ, ∃ (_ : Function.Surjective ⇑φ), ∃ x, (f.val.app (op S')) x = (Y.val.map (op φ)) y

explanatories.CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.HasFunct: This definition describes the property that every morphism in a concrete category can be decomposed into a surjective map followed by an injective map in a functorial manner.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget: This definition describes a forgetful functor that maps objects from a concrete category to their underlying types in a specific universe.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Condensed.epi_iff_locallySurjective_on_c.description: This theorem states that a morphism in a category of condensed objects is an epimorphism if and only if it is locally surjective on compact Hausdorff spaces.

Condensed.epi_iff_surjective_on_stonean.code:
Condensed.epi_iff_surjective_on_stonean.{u, u', v'} (A : Type u') [Category.{v', u'} A] [ConcreteCategory A]
  [HasFunctorialSurjectiveInjectiveFactorization A] [PreservesFiniteProducts (CategoryTheory.forget A)]
  [∀ (X : CompHausᵒᵖ), HasLimitsOfShape (StructuredArrow X Stonean.toCompHaus.op) A] {X Y : Condensed A} (f : X ⟶ Y)
  [(extensiveTopology Stonean).WEqualsLocallyBijective A] [HasSheafify (extensiveTopology Stonean) A]
  [(extensiveTopology Stonean).HasSheafCompose (CategoryTheory.forget A)]
  [Balanced (Sheaf (extensiveTopology Stonean) A)] :
  Epi f ↔ ∀ (S : Stonean), Function.Surjective ⇑(f.val.app (op S.compHaus))

explanatories.CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.HasFunct: This definition describes the property that every morphism in a concrete category can be decomposed into a surjective map followed by an injective map in a functorial manner.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget: This definition describes a forgetful functor that maps objects from a concrete category to their underlying types in a specific universe.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Condensed.epi_iff_surjective_on_stonean.description: This theorem asserts that a morphism in a category of condensed objects is an epimorphism if and only if it is surjective when evaluated on all Stonean spaces.

LightCondensed.code: LightCondensed.{u, v, w} (C : Type w) [Category.{v, w} C] : Type (max (max (max (u + 1) w) u) v)
LightCondensed.comment:
`LightCondensed.{u} C` is the category of light condensed objects in a category `C`, which are
defined as sheaves on `LightProfinite.{u}` with respect to the coherent Grothendieck topology.
LightCondensed.fullDefinition: def LightCondensed (C : Type w) [Category.{v} C] :=   Sheaf (coherentTopology LightProfinite.{u}) C
LightCondensed.description: This defines a category comprising light condensed objects that can be characterized as sheaves over a specific profinite category with a coherent topology.

LightCondensed.discrete.code:
LightCondensed.discrete.{u, w} (C : Type w) [Category.{u, w} C] [HasSheafify (coherentTopology LightProfinite) C] :
  C ⥤ LightCondensed C
LightCondensed.discrete.comment: The discrete condensed object associated to an object of `C` is the constant sheaf at that object.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.constantSheaf: This defines a functor that assigns to each object of a category a constant sheaf formed by the sheafification of the constant presheaf at that object within a given Grothendieck topology.

LightCondensed.discrete.fullDefinition: noncomputable def LightCondensed.discrete : C ⥤ LightCondensed.{u} C := constantSheaf _ C
LightCondensed.discrete.description: This establishes a functor that associates each object in a category with its corresponding discrete condensed object viewed as a constant sheaf.

LightCondensed.underlying.code: LightCondensed.underlying.{u, w} (C : Type w) [Category.{u, w} C] : LightCondensed C ⥤ C
LightCondensed.underlying.comment:
The underlying object of a condensed object in `C` is the condensed object evaluated at a point.
This can be viewed as a sort of forgetful functor from `Condensed C` to `C`

explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.LightProfinite.of: This definition creates a light profinite space from any type that is equipped with the structures of a compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected, and second countable topological space.

LightCondensed.underlying.fullDefinition: noncomputable def LightCondensed.underlying : LightCondensed.{u} C ⥤ C :=   (sheafSections _ _).obj (op (LightProfinite.of PUnit))
LightCondensed.underlying.description: This defines a functor that extracts the underlying object from a condensed object by evaluating it at a specific point.

LightCondSet.discrete.comment: A version of `LightCondensed.discrete` in the `LightCondSet` namespace

explanatories.LightCondensed.discrete: This establishes a functor that associates each object in a category with its corresponding discrete condensed object viewed as a constant sheaf.

LightCondSet.discrete.description: This defines a functor that provides a discrete condensed object for each type in the context of light condensed sets.

LightCondSet.underlying.comment: A version of `LightCondensed.underlying` in the `LightCondSet` namespace

explanatories.LightCondensed.underlying: This defines a functor that extracts the underlying object from a condensed object by evaluating it at a specific point.

LightCondSet.underlying.description: This defines a functor that retrieves the underlying type from a condensed object within the framework of light condensed sets.

LightCondensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj.code:
LightCondensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj.{u, w} (C : Type w) [Category.{u, w} C]
  [HasSheafify (coherentTopology LightProfinite) C] : LightCondensed.discrete C ⊣ LightCondensed.underlying C
LightCondensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj.comment:
Discreteness is left adjoint to the forgetful functor. When `C` is `Type*`, this is analogous to
`TopCat.adj₁ : TopCat.discrete ⊣ forget TopCat`.

explanatories.LightCondensed.underlying: This defines a functor that extracts the underlying object from a condensed object by evaluating it at a specific point.
explanatories.LightProfinite.isTerminalPUnit: This definition states that the one-element space is a terminal object in the category of light profinite spaces.
explanatories.LightCondSet.discrete: This defines a functor that provides a discrete condensed object for each type in the context of light condensed sets.
explanatories.LightCondSet.underlying: This defines a functor that retrieves the underlying type from a condensed object within the framework of light condensed sets.

LightCondensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj.fullDefinition: noncomputable def LightCondensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj : discrete C ⊣ underlying C :=   constantSheafAdj _ _ LightProfinite.isTerminalPUnit
LightCondensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj.description: This establishes an adjunction between the functor that assigns a discrete condensed object to any category and the functor that retrieves the underlying object from a condensed object.

LightCondMod.comment:
The category of condensed `R`-modules, defined as sheaves of `R`-modules over
`CompHaus` with respect to the coherent Grothendieck topology.
LightCondMod.description: This defines the category of condensed modules over a ring, which are structured as sheaves of modules within a specific Grothendieck topology.

LightCondensed.free.code: LightCondensed.free.{u} (R : Type u) [Ring R] : LightCondSet ⥤ LightCondMod R
LightCondensed.free.comment: The left adjoint to the forgetful functor. The *free condensed `R`-module* on a condensed set.

explanatories.LightCondMod: This defines the category of condensed modules over a ring, which are structured as sheaves of modules within a specific Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.composeAndSheafify: This definition introduces a functor that transforms a sheaf in one category into a sheaf in another category by composing it with a functor and sheafifying the result.
explanatories.ModuleCat.free: This definition represents a functor that constructs free modules over a ring from types by associating each type element with a generator of the module.

LightCondensed.free.fullDefinition: def LightCondensed.free : LightCondSet ⥤ LightCondMod R :=   Sheaf.composeAndSheafify _ (ModuleCat.free R)
LightCondensed.free.description: This defines the free condensed module over a condensed set, serving as the left adjoint to the forgetful functor.

LightCondensed.forget.code: LightCondensed.forget.{u} (R : Type u) [Ring R] : LightCondMod R ⥤ LightCondSet
LightCondensed.forget.comment: The forgetful functor from condensed `R`-modules to condensed sets.

explanatories.LightCondMod: This defines the category of condensed modules over a ring, which are structured as sheaves of modules within a specific Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.sheafCompose: The definition establishes a functor that connects the categories of sheaves for two different types based on a functor that supports composition for a given Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget: This definition describes a forgetful functor that maps objects from a concrete category to their underlying types in a specific universe.

LightCondensed.forget.fullDefinition: def LightCondensed.forget : LightCondMod R ⥤ LightCondSet :=   sheafCompose _ (CategoryTheory.forget _)
LightCondensed.forget.description: This defines the forgetful functor that maps condensed modules over a ring to condensed sets.

LightCondAb.comment:
The category of condensed abelian groups, defined as sheaves of abelian groups over
`CompHaus` with respect to the coherent Grothendieck topology.

explanatories.LightCondMod: This defines the category of condensed modules over a ring, which are structured as sheaves of modules within a specific Grothendieck topology.

LightCondAb.description: This defines the category of condensed abelian groups, which are structured as sheaves of abelian groups within a specific Grothendieck topology.

lightProfiniteToLightCondSet.comment: The functor from `LightProfinite.{u}` to `LightCondSet.{u}` given by the Yoneda sheaf.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Subcanonical.yoneda: This definition provides a Yoneda functor that maps a category into the sheaf category under a subcanonical Grothendieck topology.

lightProfiniteToLightCondSet.description: This defines a functor that maps from the category of light profinite spaces to the category of light condensed sets, utilizing the Yoneda sheaf construction.

LightCondensed.ofSheafLightProfinite.code:
LightCondensed.ofSheafLightProfinite.{u, u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} A] (F : LightProfiniteᵒᵖ ⥤ A)
  [PreservesFiniteProducts F] (hF : EqualizerCondition F) : LightCondensed A
LightCondensed.ofSheafLightProfinite.comment:
The light condensed object associated to a presheaf on `LightProfinite` which preserves finite
products and satisfies the equalizer condition.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.regularTopology.Equalizer: A contravariant functor is said to satisfy the Equalizer Condition if it maps kernel pairs of effective epimorphisms to equalizer diagrams.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_pres: This theorem states that a presheaf is a sheaf with respect to a coherent topology if and only if it satisfies conditions related to preserving finite products and the equalizer condition under specific assumptions on the underlying category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.val: This definition specifies the functor representing the underlying presheaf of a given sheaf with respect to a specified Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cond: This theorem states that a sheaf associated with a Grothendieck topology is characterized by its underlying presheaf satisfying the sheaf condition for that topology.

LightCondensed.ofSheafLightProfinite.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofSheafLightProfinite (F : LightProfinite.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ A) [PreservesFiniteProducts F]     (hF : EqualizerCondition F) : LightCondensed A where   val := F   cond := by     rw [isSheaf_iff_preservesFiniteProducts_and_equalizerCondition F]     exact ⟨⟨⟨fun _ _ ↦ inferInstance⟩⟩, hF⟩
LightCondensed.ofSheafLightProfinite.description: This defines a light condensed object derived from a presheaf on a specific category, given that it preserves finite products and meets the equalizer condition.

LightCondMod.ofSheafLightProfinite.code:
LightCondMod.ofSheafLightProfinite.{u} (R : Type u) [Ring R] (F : LightProfiniteᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat R)
  [PreservesFiniteProducts F] (hF : EqualizerCondition F) : LightCondMod R

explanatories.CategoryTheory.regularTopology.Equalizer: A contravariant functor is said to satisfy the Equalizer Condition if it maps kernel pairs of effective epimorphisms to equalizer diagrams.
explanatories.LightCondensed.ofSheafLightProfinite: This defines a light condensed object derived from a presheaf on a specific category, given that it preserves finite products and meets the equalizer condition.

LightCondMod.ofSheafLightProfinite.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev ofSheafLightProfinite (F : LightProfinite.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R)     [PreservesFiniteProducts F] (hF : EqualizerCondition F) : LightCondMod.{u} R :=   LightCondensed.ofSheafLightProfinite F hF
LightCondMod.ofSheafLightProfinite.description: This defines a light condensed module associated with a presheaf on a category, contingent upon preserving finite products and satisfying the equalizer condition.

TopCat.toLightCondSet.comment:
Associate to a `u`-small topological space the corresponding light condensed set, given by
`yonedaPresheaf`.

explanatories.equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf: This theorem demonstrates that under certain conditions on a category and its morphisms, the Yoneda presheaf satisfies the equalizer condition necessary to qualify as a sheaf for the regular topology.
explanatories.LightProfinite.effectiveEpi_iff_surjecti: An effective epimorphism in light profinite spaces is equivalent to being a surjective function.
explanatories.QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous: This theorem states that a continuous surjective map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space qualifies as a quotient map.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.continuous: This theorem states that a continuous map between two topological spaces induces a continuous function when viewed as a function.

TopCat.toLightCondSet.fullDefinition: noncomputable def TopCat.toLightCondSet (X : TopCat.{u}) : LightCondSet.{u} :=   @LightCondSet.ofSheafLightProfinite (yonedaPresheaf LightProfinite.toTopCat.{u} X) _ (by     apply equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf LightProfinite.toTopCat.{u} X     intro Z B π he     rw [LightProfinite.effectiveEpi_iff_surjective] at he     apply QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous he π.continuous)
TopCat.toLightCondSet.description: This defines a mapping that associates a small topological space with its corresponding light condensed set via a specific construction.

factorsThrough_of_pullbackCondition.comment:
An auxiliary lemma to that allows us to use `QuotientMap.lift` in the proof of
`equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullback: This definition specifies the property of a category having a pullback for a given pair of morphisms from two objects to a common object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst: This definition describes the first projection map from the pullback object associated with a pair of morphisms to the first object of one of the morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd: This definition specifies the morphism from the pullback object to one of its original objects, representing the second projection of the pullback for a given pair of morphisms.
explanatories.Function.FactorsThrough: This defines a concept where one function can be said to factor through another if equal outputs of the second function imply equal outputs of the first function.

factorsThrough_of_pullbackCondition.description: This lemma establishes a condition under which a morphism factors through another morphism in the context of a pullback in a category, given certain assumptions about the morphisms involved and their properties.

equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf.code:
equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf.{w, w', v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (G : C ⥤ TopCat) (X : Type w')
  [TopologicalSpace X] [(Z B : C) → (π : Z ⟶ B) → [inst : EffectiveEpi π] → PreservesLimit (cospan π π) G]
  (hq : ∀ (Z B : C) (π : Z ⟶ B) [inst : EffectiveEpi π], QuotientMap ⇑(G.map π)) :
  EqualizerCondition (yonedaPresheaf G X)
equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf.comment:
If `G` preserves the relevant pullbacks and every effective epi in `C` is a quotient map (which is
the case when `C` is `CompHaus` or `Profinite`), then `yonedaPresheaf` satisfies the equalizer
condition which is required to be a sheaf for the regular topology.

explanatories.QuotientMap: A function between topological spaces is defined as a quotient map if it is surjective and the openness of sets is preserved through its preimages.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.regularTopology.Equalizer: A contravariant functor is said to satisfy the Equalizer Condition if it maps kernel pairs of effective epimorphisms to equalizer diagrams.

equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf.description: This theorem demonstrates that under certain conditions on a category and its morphisms, the Yoneda presheaf satisfies the equalizer condition necessary to qualify as a sheaf for the regular topology.

TopCat.toCondensedSet.comment:
Associate to a `(u+1)`-small topological space the corresponding condensed set, given by
`yonedaPresheaf`.

explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Bool.true: The statement identifies the boolean value representing true, which is distinct from the logical proposition denoting truth.
explanatories.equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf: This theorem demonstrates that under certain conditions on a category and its morphisms, the Yoneda presheaf satisfies the equalizer condition necessary to qualify as a sheaf for the regular topology.
explanatories.CompHaus.effectiveEpi_tfae: In the category of compact Hausdorff spaces, having a morphism that is an effective epimorphism, an epimorphism, and a surjective function are equivalent properties.
explanatories.QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous: This theorem states that a continuous surjective map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space qualifies as a quotient map.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.continuous: This theorem states that a continuous map between two topological spaces induces a continuous function when viewed as a function.

TopCat.toCondensedSet.fullDefinition: noncomputable def TopCat.toCondensedSet (X : TopCat.{u+1}) : CondensedSet.{u} :=   @CondensedSet.ofSheafCompHaus (yonedaPresheaf.{u, u+1, u, u+1} compHausToTop.{u} X) _ (by     apply (config := { allowSynthFailures := true }) equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf       compHausToTop.{u} X     intro Z B π he     rw [((CompHaus.effectiveEpi_tfae π).out 0 2 :)] at he     apply QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous he π.continuous )
TopCat.toCondensedSet.description: This definition establishes a method for associating a compact condensed set to a small topological space through the Yoneda presheaf construction.
